paragraphs: GEOSATIS makes a GPS ankle bracelet called the ODIN-i. The company presents itself as a supplier of monitoring solutions aimed at public safety.

The bracelet is described as installing or removing in under twenty seconds. It uses no straps, no tools and no tether. It can also be opened remotely from the software. A radio-frequency transmitter called Beacon communicates with the bracelet to supply consistent indoor location information. A separate app is meant to give victims and organizations an early warning when an offender is in proximity. That app carries a one-touch emergency call and panic button.

For support, the company points to a worldwide knowledge base and skilled team members. It also claims operational cost savings achieved through increased efficiency, streamlined processes and resource optimization.
